findings.finding: The FY27 adjusted PBT guide ('in line with consensus', GBP58.2m average) was set on 28 April on three months of flat ex-Funky Pigeon sales. It predates a high-street run of -1.5% (May), -6.2% (June) and -3.8% (July) year on year, in-store non-food at -1.9% in July and -1.2% in August, and Asia-Europe freight still near $3.5k per 40ft into late September. The interims must restate the guide, and the balance of risk is a softer steer (lower half or 'challenging') rather than a raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance-line surprises on this name have been large and negative: the Dec 2025 FY26 cut moved -27.39% (Trading Statement 2025-12-12), and the Sep 2024 half-year, which carried a softer outlook, moved -21.12%. The Sep 2025 half-year, with the FY guide unchanged, moved -3.78%, and the Jan 2026 statement reiterating the revised guide moved +0.43%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is 72.8p, below the ~96p held before the Dec warning and a little above the May-June ~67p low, at about 6.5x FY26 adjusted EPS of 11.8p, so the market already discounts a weak consumer. What is not visible is a trimmed guide: the short register is flat at 2.48% rather than building, the 5-day run-up is +4.15%, and the only public H1 bar (~2.3p EPS) is an aggregator figure. If a cut were priced, shorts would be adding and the price would sit at or below the May low. Footfall-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company says it, which is why this is sized well below the -9% median move for a guidance change.
findings.independence: The macro inputs are independent of the company document: BRC-Sensormatic high-street footfall, May -1.5% (https://brc.org.uk/news-and-events/news/corporate-affairs/2026/ungated/footfall-hit-by-record-sunshine/), July -3.8% after June -6.2% (https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/08/footfall-brc-july-2026/); BRC-KPMG in-store non-food -1.9% in July (https://retailrewired.co.uk/2026/08/11/soaring-temperatures-cool-consumer-demand-as-retail-sales-edge-up-just-1-3-yoy-in-july/); Drewry WCI Shanghai-Rotterdam $3,485 per 40ft on 24 Sep 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-24-september-2026); Berenberg's May 2026 downgrade on H2 caution (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/why-card-factory-lse-card-080914462.html). All are proxies, none is a company number.

findings.finding: The Wellcome Trust's stake (4.93% on 19 Aug) was sold down to 0% by 21 Sep 2026, and Aberforth Partners took its holding from 10.074% (14 Sep) to 11.045% and then 14.746% (21 Sep, 48.75m shares), apparently absorbing the block. Together with the running buyback (524,643 shares in 21-25 Sep), the pre-print overhang is gone and a value holder has added into the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance on this name of a large holder change right before results; the shares rose 4.15% over the 5 sessions to the seal as the block cleared.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced already: the 5-day run-up of +4.15% is the overhang clearing. What is left is that a supply source is gone for print day and a 14.7% value holder is less likely to sell into a soft outlook. Aberforth has no inside information, so this says nothing about the numbers and is sized small.
findings.independence: Wellcome's disposal to 0.000% on 21 Sep is a separate TR-1 (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/card-factory--card/holding-s-in-company/9786431), and the buyback is shown in the Transaction in Own Shares RNS (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/card-factory--card/transaction-in-own-shares/9792600). All come from the same issuer channel.

outside_window.finding: The 2026 AGM (25 Jun) re-elected the Chair (74.26%), CEO (75.63%) and CFO (75.63%) with about 46-49m votes against, and both pre-emption disapplication resolutions failed. The board owes a shareholder-engagement update within six months, i.e. by about 25 Dec 2026. Aberforth has since become the largest holder at 14.7%. Governance or capital-allocation change is possible later, and it is not dated into this window unless the interims carry it.

lessons_applied: 'Two findings resting on one document are one finding' and 'narrow proxy loses to broad series': the draft's separate H1 reported-quarter finding (-0.7) rested on the same footfall series as the guidance finding. It was merged into the guidance finding, and the H1 line moved to new_in_release, because the H1 bar is only an aggregator figure and 'reported_quarter findings went 4 of 14'.

'The move is in the guide' and 'you were right about the number and too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 7.5 to 8.0 (numbers new, guidance restatement possible, thin $0.93m/day name); the guidance finding kept its size, -1.2 to -1.3.
